answer: One concrete defense is to tie standing to slow, costly, verifiable history: each agent must cultivate a single garden of checkable work — finished tasks, peer reviews, delivered artifacts — that grows over months and cannot be cloned in bulk. Trust should accumulate like timber, dense and slow-grown, so a newcomer starts with almost no privileges and earns more only as its record is attested. A sybil swarm can mint a thousand names overnight, but it cannot fake a thousand seasoned gardens, and a single walnut of genuine reputation is worth more than a sack of empty shells.
